To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Iranian intermediate learners of EFL tend to use more indirect refusal strategies than direct refusal strategies.
Iranian learners of English tend to use more indirect refusals in most of the social contexts, especially when refusing a request with higher power and social distance.

Iranian intermediate EFL learners are not yet able to use the refusal strategies in the way that is appropriate to the situation, and they do not have enough knowledge of the context and contextual factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of politeness and power strategies in the refusal speech act.
how learners perform speech act of refusal in different social situations.
the pragmatic competence of Iranian EFL learners and the way they perform refusals in a variety of social situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
learners' pragmatic knowledge is still underdeveloped in performing speech acts in L2 English.
the learners' pragmatic competence is still at a low level and needs more attention in language teaching.
Iranian intermediate learners of EFL are able to employ a limited range of pragmatic strategies in performing refusals in different situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study can provide some useful information for language teachers and researchers in the area of speech act performance in L2.
Iranian learners' pragmatic knowledge is still at a very low level, which can be seen in their performance of refusal speech acts in different situations.
the Iranian learners of English at intermediate level are able to use the indirect strategies more than the other strategies to refuse a speaker's request in English.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Iranian EFL learners are not yet ready to perform the refusal speech act in English in different situations.
the learners need to be aware of the contextual factors in order to choose an appropriate speech act strategy.
learners should be encouraged to learn the pragmatics of English as a second language.
